line: Average attention on one screen: 2.5 minutes in 2004. Now, 47 seconds.
Imagine two students. One daydreams of a swan, and falls behind.
Thais say: grab two fish at once, and you may catch neither.
A Zen master's practice: when hungry, I eat. When tired, I sleep.
To focus deeper, don't just see the ball. Watch its spinning seams.
credit: W. Timothy Gallwey · Inner Game of Tennis

line: Better basketball shooters held a still gaze on the hoop longer.
Long before basketball, the Gita taught: sit still, eyes on nose tip.
Bringing wandering attention back, again and again, is the root of willpower.
Yoga has a word for holding the mind in place: dharana.
So in every Sun Salutation, never forget drishti (gaze), bandhas and breath.
